quizzes.stem: An AI application connects to a ticketing system and a document store, both exposed through MCP. How is the connecting side organized?

options.a: A single client multiplexes both servers over one shared connection
options.b: The host talks to each server directly, with no client component
options.c: Each server creates a client inside itself to call the application back
options.d: The host creates one client for each server, each with a dedicated link

explanation.d: The page says "The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server", and that each client "maintains a dedicated connection with its corresponding MCP server".
explanation.a: Ruled out because each client "maintains a dedicated connection with its corresponding MCP server", so none is shared.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the client is "A component that maintains a connection to an MCP server and obtains context from an MCP server for the MCP host to use".
explanation.c: Ruled out because it is the host that does the creating: "The MCP host accomplishes this by creating one MCP client for each MCP server".

quizzes.stem: A developer offers three things: a function the model may call to book flights, a read-only data document that the application attaches as context, and a ready-made instruction that a user selects from a menu. Which primitives fit, in that order?

options.a: A prompt, a tool, a resource
options.b: A resource, a prompt, a tool
options.c: A tool, a prompt, a resource
options.d: A tool, a resource, a prompt

explanation.d: A function the model calls is a tool, because tools "are model-controlled, meaning AI models can discover and invoke them automatically". Read-only data that the application attaches is a resource, which the application "can access this information directly and decide how to use it". A template that a person picks is a prompt.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a resource is the one the application "can access this information directly and decide how to use it", so it cannot stand for the function the model calls.
explanation.b: Ruled out because tools "are model-controlled, meaning AI models can discover and invoke them automatically", so the first item is a tool.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the data document is a resource, which gives "read-only access to information", and the menu item is a prompt.

quizzes.stem: How does a client written for the 2026-07-28 revision tell a server which protocol version it speaks?

options.a: An initialize exchange that opens a session and fixes it for later calls
options.b: A header on the first call only, which the server remembers afterwards
options.c: A mandatory discovery call that must precede every other call
options.d: Each call carries it in its metadata field, with no opening handshake

explanation.d: The page says "Every request declares the protocol version it is using" in its metadata field, and that the server "accepts or rejects each request independently".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the legacy versions "establish a session with an initialize handshake", and the modern ones have none.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the server "accepts or rejects each request independently", so nothing is remembered from a first call.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a client "is free to invoke any RPC inline", so discovery is optional.

quizzes.stem: A stdio server prints a debug line with the language's ordinary print function, and the client then fails to parse the stream. Why?

options.a: The client reads standard error as well, and treats any text there as fatal
options.b: Printed lines are queued and delivered after the tool call has ended
options.c: The SDK forbids logging libraries, so every debug line is rejected
options.d: Standard output carries only protocol messages, so stray text corrupts it

explanation.d: The page says "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the client "SHOULD NOT assume stderr output indicates error conditions".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the stream carries one message per line and "The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message", with no queue of printed lines.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the guide says to use a logger that writes to stderr: "Never write to stdout. Writing to stdout will corrupt the JSON-RPC messages and break your server."

quizzes.stem: A search tool receives a date range in the wrong format, and the server wants the model to try again with a fix. How should the failure be reported?

options.a: As a JSON-RPC error response, which is passed to the model for retries
options.b: As a protocol error that says the request itself is malformed
options.c: By returning empty text, which signals the model to ask the user
options.d: As an ordinary result flagged as an error, with a readable explanation

explanation.d: The page says tool execution errors "contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct and retry with adjusted parameters", and lists "Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)" among them.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Clients MAY provide protocol errors to language models, though these are less likely to result in successful recovery."
explanation.b: Ruled out because a wrong format is an "Input validation errors (e.g., date in wrong format, value out of range)", which is a tool execution error and not a malformed request.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Clients SHOULD provide tool execution errors to language models to enable self-correction", which needs text that says what to change.

quizzes.stem: A tool declares that it only reads data, and a client skips the confirmation prompt for it because of that declaration. What does the specification say about trusting the declaration?

options.a: Hints are binding, so a read-only tool never needs confirmation
options.b: Hints are checked by the SDK, which blocks any tool that writes
options.c: Hints are trusted once the first call has succeeded without an error
options.d: Hints are unverified claims, unless the origin is vetted

explanation.d: The page quotes the specification: "clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations".
explanation.b: Ruled out because annotations are only "Optional properties describing tool behavior" and nothing in the SDK enforces them.
explanation.c: Ruled out because trust depends on where the server comes from, "unless they come from trusted servers", and not on how a first call went.

quizzes.stem: A server's tools are not showing up in a host, and the team cannot tell why. Which first step does the documentation recommend?

options.a: Reinstall the host application, since a corrupt cache hides tools
options.b: Write the server again in another language to rule out an SDK defect there
options.c: Add output to stdout so that the host can see the server's progress
options.d: Try it standalone in the Inspector, with no other application involved

explanation.d: The page says "Test it standalone with the Inspector" is one of the documented steps and that the guide calls it "This should be your first stop."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the documented steps check the server rather than the host: "Verify server process is running".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the steps go through logs, the process and "Test standalone with Inspector" before anything is rewritten.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Local MCP servers should not log messages to stdout (standard out), as this will interfere with protocol operation."

quizzes.stem: A stdio server started by a host cannot find credentials that work in the developer's shell. Which documented behavior explains it?

options.a: The host wipes the whole environment on purpose, to keep secrets away from servers
options.b: Credentials are read from the shell only when the transport used is HTTP
options.c: The server receives its variables only after the first tool call has arrived
options.d: Only a limited subset is inherited, so extra variables go in the config

explanation.d: The page quotes the guide: "MCP servers launched over stdio inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically (the exact set is platform-dependent)."
explanation.a: Ruled out because servers "inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically", which is some of them, not none.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the fix is to "set an env key in the host's configuration", whatever the transport.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the variables are fixed when the process is launched: "MCP servers launched over stdio inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically".

quizzes.stem: A CI job must exercise a server without a browser and print machine-readable results. Which Inspector client fits?

options.a: The web one, run headless with the default settings
options.b: The terminal-UI one, since it prints results as JSON
options.c: None, because the Inspector can only run interactively
options.d: The scriptable command-line mode, built for pipelines

explanation.d: The page's table says the CLI is "A scriptable, machine-readable client for CI, shell pipelines, and coding agents."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the web one is "A full graphical inspector in the browser. The default, and the richest surface."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the terminal one is "An interactive terminal UI, for when a browser isn't available or wanted."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the CLI is "A scriptable, machine-readable client for CI, shell pipelines, and coding agents."

quizzes.stem: A server works in the Inspector, but the host cannot start it from its configuration file, which gives a relative path to the data folder. What does the documentation blame?

options.a: A host can launch only servers that were first registered with the Inspector
options.b: Relative paths can resolve only when the server runs over Streamable HTTP
options.c: A host can pass along no environment variables, so the data path is lost
options.d: The directory can be undefined, so locations should be written in full

explanation.d: The third page quotes the guide: the directory of a launched server "may be undefined (like / on macOS) since the client could be started from anywhere", so use absolute paths.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the guide says "the same principles apply to any stdio-based MCP client", and no registration with the Inspector exists.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "testing from the command line uses the directory where you run the command", which is the contrast, and the transport is not part of it.
explanation.c: Ruled out because servers "inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically", which is some of them and not none.

quizzes.stem: Under the 2026-07-28 revision, a server needs to ask the user a question in the middle of a call, but the incoming call declared no matching feature. What does the server return?

options.a: An unsupported-version error that lists the versions it accepts
options.b: An invalid-params error, since the metadata fields are absent
options.c: A tool result flagged as an error, saying the user cannot be reached
options.d: A missing-capability error, naming whatever the metadata omitted

explanation.d: The third page says that if the server needs a capability that the request's client capabilities did not declare, "it returns a MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (code -32021) naming the missing capabilities".
explanation.a: Ruled out because an unsupported-version error is one that "lists the server's supported versions in its data field", and the version was fine here.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A request missing either required field is rejected with error -32602", and the required fields were sent.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the error is "returned as an error with its own code", so a client can tell it from a failed tool.

quizzes.stem: A team must build an MCP server that speaks the newest protocol version. Which of the four SDKs used in the course reached that version when it was checked?

options.a: All four, since they share one specification and release together
options.b: Only the Kotlin library, because it is the newest of the four
options.c: Only the Java library, which the documentation ranks in its top tier overall
options.d: Only the Python library; the other three stop at an earlier revision

explanation.d: The first page says the Python SDK speaks both eras, and that the other three "contain no support for 2026-07-28, and their latest revision is 2025-11-25".
explanation.a: Ruled out because three of them "contain no support for 2026-07-28".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the Kotlin SDK is one of the three whose "latest revision is 2025-11-25".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Java is Tier 2 and Kotlin is Tier 3", and the Java SDK stops at the earlier revision as well.

quizzes.stem: A query matches no stored entries. How does the course's notes server answer?

options.a: With a tool error that tells the model to ask the user for a new query
options.b: With a protocol error, as for an unknown tool, so that the client logs it
options.c: With a resource error for the missing note, as for a bad id
options.d: With ordinary text saying that nothing fits, and the error flag stays off

explanation.d: The third page says that with no match the search answers `No notes match "{query}"`, "which is not an error".
explanation.a: Ruled out because the answer is "which is not an error", so there is no tool error to read.
explanation.b: Ruled out because protocol errors "indicate issues with the request structure itself that models are less likely to be able to fix", and the request here is valid.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the protocol error that says `No note {id}` is "for reading a note that does not exist", and "a search that finds nothing is a normal answer".
